summary: KV cache serialization spike causes backpressure and client timeouts on deep prompts with high max_tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LumaDocs reports repeated request timeouts (504 / client disconnects) when sending prompts with very large context + max_tokens=120000 via the Redwood hosted API. Occurs primarily for streams that use function-calling and chunked streaming.

Impact:
- Several production API calls for LumaDocs are timing out during long-document summarization jobs, causing failed jobs and user-facing errors.
- Error rate ~12% for affected routes over a 6-hour window; spikes align with heavy serialization activity on the serving nodes.

Environment:
- Hosted (Redwood managed), dedicated tenant for LumaDocs
- Region: us-east
- Models: redwood-alpha-1 (default), gptj-6b used for fallback testing

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send a streaming generation request with a prompt consisting of concatenated OCRed pages (~90k tokens) plus system instructions (function-calls enabled).
2) Set max_tokens to 120000 and enable streaming with chunk_size=1024.
3) Observe response flow: initial tokens stream, then long pause (~20-60s), then 504 or client disconnect.

Observed behavior:
- Serving-runtime logs show a sharp CPU spike on the inference host coincident with a call to kv-cache serialize/flush.
- During the spike, the request is held in the finalizer queue; downstream router returns 504 or the client times out.
- When reproducing in a dedicated test cluster, increasing the CPU limit on the host delays but does not eliminate timeouts.

Expected behavior:
- Long-context requests should stream tokens progressively; KV cache maintenance should not block final token flushing or cause client-visible timeouts.

Logs and traces:
- Sample trace: https://observability.internal/redwood/traces/trace-2025-01-17-22abcd
- Example serving log excerpt: 
  [2025-01-17T16:42:12Z] INFO finalizer: start finalize request SUP-531907-ctx-123
  [2025-01-17T16:42:30Z] WARN kv-cache: beginning bulk-serialize (size=512MB, entries=19278)
  [2025-01-17T16:42:55Z] ERROR api-gateway: upstream timeout after 30s while waiting for response
  [2025-01-17T16:43:02Z] INFO finalizer: aborted due to client disconnect

Additional notes:
- No concurrent autoscaler events recorded for the node.
- Node has nvme-backed local disk; serialization writes are synchronous to disk in current runtime build.
steps_to_reproduce: Prepare prompt: aggregate ~90k tokens of context (e.g., 100 pages OCR text).
Issue streaming generation call to /v1/generate with model=redwood-alpha-1, max_tokens=120000, streaming=true, chunk_size=1024, function_call enabled.
Observe token stream for ~10-20s, then long pause and eventual 504 or client disconnect.
comments: 2025-01-17 17:05 - Support (Ava): Acknowledged with customer, collected request ids and sample payloads. Escalating to infra on-call.
2025-01-17 17:22 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced on dedicated repro cluster. Observed large synchronous KV serialization spikes. Adding as investigation owner.

2025-01-17 18:10 - Support (Ava): Provided customer with temporary mitigation: reduce max_tokens to 40k OR disable function-calls for long-document summarization. Customer confirms reduced error rate but requires long-term fix.

2025-01-18 09:30 - Eng (Priya Rao): Hypothesis - synchronous kv-cache flush runs on finalizer thread causing blocking; propose async background serialization and streaming of final tokens before flush.
2025-01-19 11:15 - Eng (Diego): Deployed config change to defer KV flush until post-response for a subset of traffic (canary). Observed drop in 504s for canary traffic from 11% to 1.5%.
2025-01-20 08:05 - Support (Ava): Customer accepted the canary behavior as interim; requested ETA for full fix and follow-up on SLA impact.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis validated: bulk synchronous KV serialization on finalize path is the root trigger for CPU spike and blocking behavior.
Reproducible locally with the same model and payload sizes. Profiling shows finalize thread spends ~25s in serialization (memcpy + compression) before returning.

Alternative mitigations tried: increasing finalize thread pool size reduces collisions but increases memory pressure; streaming token pacing reduces visibility of spikes but is not acceptable for customer's latency needs.
Canary config (defer-kv-flush=true) routed 5% of LumaDocs traffic; telemetry shows 90th/95th percentile token latency improved and timeout rate dropped substantially in canary.
Related internal ticket: INT-8842 tracking runtime rewrite for background KV compaction and non-blocking finalizer.
Trigger conditions: payloads > ~50k tokens and aggressive max_tokens (>100k) with chunked streaming and function-call serialization tend to hit this path.
resolution:
Interim: Enabled defer-kv-flush=true canary for LumaDocs and similar heavy long-context tenants; customer accepted as short-term mitigation. Workaround documented: reduce max_tokens, increase chunk_size to 4096, or disable function-calls for massive documents.

Permanent: Engineering PR landed to implement asynchronous KV serialization and streaming-first finalizer behavior (see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2784). Rollout plan: staged canaries across regions, monitor timeout rates and CPU/memory pressure, full rollout targeted for 2025-02-05.

Postmortem action items created: INT-8842 (runtime refactor), DOC-124 (customer-facing guidance on long-context best practices), and add automated regression tests for >50k token flows in CI.
